[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James was born in 1730. He is the son of [[Mangan-824|Catherine Glasco]].

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasco-146]] is assessed at 12% (uncertain). The held Dublin will account leaves James as a possible son of Catherine or brother of Philip the elder. Making Philip-146 his father selects a less-supported alternative, and the estimated 1730/1715 births would imply fatherhood at about15. Those estimates are not exact exclusions, but the competing sibling reconstruction is materially stronger.

Uncertain12%; existing father retained without turning an index party or an estimated birth into a proved parent.

Next useful test: Read the 1793 Temple Street carpenter’s will for explicit kinship.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasco-148 WikiTree profile export for Glasco-148]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Possible James Glasco of Omagh ===
The 1786 marriage column names James Glasco, Omagh publican aged 61, and Jane Murray of the same place aged 16.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050075355/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1786-09-05, p.3].</ref>

Three 1793 Hope advertisements name James Glasco, Omagh, as a freight/passage contact; the 25 May issue adds a sailing delay.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021067/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-11, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021086/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-18, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/72021100/ The Northern Star, 1793-05-25, p.1].</ref>

The marriage was reported by 5 September 1786; the exact ceremony day is not given. James’s reported age suggests birth about 1724–1725. The same uncommon name and Omagh business context support, without proving, continuity with the 1793 contact. The notices do not name his parents or establish a previous marriage.

This may concern [[Glasco-148]]. Uncertain 1730 birth conflicts with the reported age by about five years; Dublin carpenter context supplies no Omagh connection, but the date is not firm.
